newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF Sakakibara says dlr comment rumour groundless.
newsitem.headline: MOF Sakakibara says dlr comment rumour groundless.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said overnight rumours that U.S. officials had told him they could tolerate the dollar at an exchange rate of 120 yen were groundless.
"Such rumours are groundless," Sakakibara told Reuters, adding that he could not comment on specific currency levels.
The dollar had risen against the yen in New York trade overnight due to the rumour, dealers said.
The U.S. currency closed in New York at 111.57/62 yen, up from 111.12/22 at the open. It was trading at around 111.42/49 yen in Tokyo morning trade.
Sakakibara also denied vague rumours, which also emerged in the U.S. markets overnight, that he had met U.S. President Bill Clinton.
